what: just qc and the code review run in parallel on the same integrated head H; the review verdict names H, not the qc status head H'; the merge ask names H' and both verdicts, and a check proves H to H' changes only the status files. A clean merge of main keeps the qc verdict when a check proves the lane's own diff is unchanged; the merge ask names the judged head, the refreshed head and the proof. The judge is a qc judge with its own role, not a code reviewer. Project rule renamed 'Review and qc judge one head'.
why: Owner ruling, issue #67 items 1, 9 and 10 (Tom, 2026-10-21): QC is every check on what ships; the code reviewer does code quality only; qc and review must not wait on each other, and a clean main refresh must not rerun the judge. Marked weakens because the review verdict no longer names the exact merge head; the status-only check carries that guarantee instead.
evidence: Two contradicting lines once this PR lands: docs/adr/0022 (corrected in place, issue #67 item 9: integrate, then qc and review in parallel, then the merge ask) and agents/qc-judge.md (the judge's own role, item 1) against issue-lifecycle#lanes-one-head 'its status-only commit is the head the fresh code review then judges' and #acceptance-qc-interim 'from a code reviewer started fresh'.

what: Parent issues and tickets live in the target's tracker, GitHub Issues or Linear; pull requests and merges stay on GitHub; a Linear lane's PR body says Tracks <KEY> (the tracker skill's pr-line) and the supervisor moves the parent and tickets to done with issue-done after merge; the qc judge runs without a tracker credential. Adds acceptance-merge-linear, acceptance-pr-tracks, acceptance-no-github-issue and story-linear-lane.
why: Owner ruling (2026-10-22, issue #82): the kit works with Linear directly so it can run on a Linear-first repository; the tracker is set per target in .octo-feather.toml, tracker work lives in packaged skills (github-pr, github-issues, linear) behind fixed script names, and ADR 0004 and 0011 were corrected in place to match.
evidence: Corrected ADR 0004 says the tracker is GitHub Issues or Linear, chosen per target, and ADR 0011 that a Linear lane's key is its lowercased ticket key, while the spec as accepted says 'A lane is one merge ask on one parent GitHub issue' (context) and 'GitHub owns parent issues, sub-issues' (boundary-github); the accepted criteria cannot pass on a Linear target.

what: A lane whose brief names no criterion (a fix to a rule an ADR or an owner ruling owns) builds none and runs no just qc: the fresh code review alone judges its integrated head, and its merge ask names that head, links the review verdict, shows checks passing and says the lane builds no criterion (Built: none, no criterion rows). Adds acceptance-merge-ask-no-criterion.
why: Owner, issue #95 (fix it rather than work around it): a lane that claims no criterion states it, and the merge-ask check then requires only the head, checks, review verdict and spec-calls items, with no just qc. One mechanism: the existing merge ask section and octo-feather-lane merge-ask, with Built: none, which the check already reads.
evidence: `octo-feather-lane merge-ask` refused PR #83 (#80), PR #90 (#84) and PR #94 (#93), lanes that build no criterion, with `criterion table: missing` and `Built: no qc: built commit on PR #N; run just qc on the lane head`; each merge ask went up with the refusal quoted (director finding 53). #lanes-one-head as accepted has every lane run just qc naming its criteria, which a lane with none cannot.

what: A ticket that serves no criterion names the rule it serves and that rule's owner, an ADR or an owner ruling, instead of a criterion id, and still ends on a demo; acceptance-one-head applies to a lane that builds at least one criterion.
why: Owner, issue #95 comments (lane #121): defect tickets whose rule an ADR or owner ruling owns cannot be filed as sub-issues. Same mechanism as the review's Check lines, `<rule> (<owner>)` (docs/adr/0008). Marked weakens: a ticket may now name no criterion, and the one-head criterion no longer covers a lane with no qc report. Out of scope: the second #95 example, a gate recipe's demo, which is the demo-surface rule (ADR 0009), a different mechanism.
evidence: `octo-feather-lane ticket` refuses a ticket naming no criterion (`class: no-criterion: no acceptance item names a criterion id`), so #121's check-scripts, check-dashes, check-refs lane-branch and integrate hand-in tickets (rules: docs/adr/0011, docs/adr/0017, owner rulings) could not be filed; and #acceptance-one-head 'the qc report named every criterion the lane builds' against #lanes-one-head's no-criterion lane, which runs no just qc.

what: just qc and the code review both run to their verdicts: one failing first never stops the other, and one implementer repairs the blocking findings of both at once before both run again in parallel on the new head.
why: Owner review comment on #lanes-one-head (2026-10-26): let both finish even if one fails first, so a second failure's problems are addressed in the same repair. Consistent with docs/adr/0022 (a failed verdict of either is a blocking finding, then both run again in parallel).
evidence: #lanes-one-head as accepted says 'neither waits for the other' and 'If either verdict fails, an implementer repairs it and both run again', which leaves open whether a failed qc or review stops the other run before it reports; the owner's review comment asks that both finish.

what: Correction lanes also start on each reflection-missed finding (fix: the question list), and the repeat count covers the director log as well as lane hand-off logs; a correction lane for a class the director reflection routed names that route. The lane close and the merge relay include the lane and director reflections.
why: Owner rulings on issue #230 (2026-10-27, 2026-10-28): the factory introspects itself without the owner as the loop: a fresh cross-family reflector (openai/gpt-6.1-sol, high) reflects at every lane close and on the director's work after each merge relay and at least daily, mines review finding classes across lanes and routes each recurring writer mistake to prevention at the writer, and a gap a reflection missed updates its question list (questions owned once, as data). Reuses pstack reflect (vendored, Pi/Herdr patch). Goes to owner review and Accept before any lane code.
evidence: issue-lifecycle#lanes-correction at main 2e1f97d starts a correction lane only on an owner correction at a gate or a class repeated across lanes, so a gap a reflection missed (issue #230 item 3) changes no question list, and nothing routes a repeated class to its writer: correction lanes #124 and #160 (duplicated-rule) closed and code review logged duplicated-rule again on gh137 and gh149.

what: Align issue-lifecycle with the accepted comms reflection triggers: the lane archive runs the lane and director reflections (the director no longer runs one after a merge), and the reflection at each archive applies the correction-lane rules and files each due correction lane's parent issue, which the director then starts; acceptance-repeat-lane's When is the next lane archive, not the director checking classes after a merge ask. Criteria unchanged in outcome.
why: Owner review of comms (2026-10-28, replies umvrhh4hh8a69 and umvrhi2azbrrm) made the reflection triggers and the correction-lane filing deterministic; owner accepted comms at c4fd14f. Director OK'd this call (4th of the lane) on 2026-10-28.
evidence: Two contradicting lines: issue-lifecycle#lc-merge at 77bae46 (director: 'after the merge checks main's CI and runs the director reflection') and #acceptance-repeat-lane ('When the director checks finding classes after the next merge ask') against comms#reflection-director at c4fd14f ('It runs at every lane archive ... The director neither starts it nor answers its questions') and comms#reflection-correction ('no agent judges whether a correction lane is due ... it files the correction lane's parent issue').

what: acceptance-qc-interim no longer requires the result to come from a qc judge started fresh and headless: each result (pass, fail or insufficient evidence) shows its evidence state, decision source and evidence record. lc-qc and qc-interim describe capture then judgment from the store; stop-qc: insufficient evidence is never triaged; spec-status-file: built entries name evidence record, capture commit and tests, built means qc passed it on captured evidence and goes stale; delivery-qa-triage adopts octo-lite's rule: a failure with complete evidence is a code fault unless a specific capture cause is named.
why: Issue #127 owner decision: the agentic judge stays only as fallback for a criterion with no runnable demo; octo-lite triage rule adopted per the owner's #127 prior-art comment.
evidence: Issue #127 evidence: #111 acceptance-prompt-eval passed 4 agentic qc runs and failed 1 on unchanged evidence; #119 the agentic judge passed quality#acceptance-judge-bench at 992344c and e826a8f and failed it at f0b50a6 on identical facts; #136 it read skills#acceptance-repo-skill-roles three ways across heads on the same recorded runs (pass 8b439fb, fail 6ad7291, fail 39e8e42). issue-lifecycle#acceptance-qc-interim requires every result from a fresh headless judge, contradicting quality#qc-judgment (judgment from the stored demo record, no judge) for a criterion with a declared demo.

what: The repeated-class trigger counts only blocking findings (code review or the product judge) of one class in the hand-off logs of two or more distinct lanes; a reflection's own finding (never blocking) and the director log make no lane due, except reflection-missed. Owner gate corrections and reflection-missed triggers unchanged.
why: Owner direction on issue #479 item 6 (correction intake, signal vs noise: raise or rethink the two-finding trigger; close what no real failure supports); owner ruling relayed by the director 2026-11-04 (Q2): count only blocking findings, in at least two distinct lanes; told to the owner at once as a weakening.
evidence: `gh issue list --state open --search '"[correction-lane" in:title'` at 2026-11-04: 157 open correction-lane issues, almost none dispatched (issue #479 item 6: about 40 filed by reflections on 2026-10-29); scripts/octo-feather-reflect at ea7d779 counts every finding line, reflection notes (blocking false) and repeats inside one lane included, REPEAT = 2.

what: Implementers run just fast before reporting; just integrate runs the fast tier on the candidate head, and the full gate only at a checkpoint (#lanes-checkpoints), recording each full pass; a red gate in either tier rolls back as before. ADR 0017 corrected in place to match.
why: Owner ruling on issue #503 (2026-11-03, 'fully agree as a priority'), with the adversarial-review consensus (comment 2026-11-03T19:44:38Z, items 2 and 3) and the owner's corrections of 2026-11-03T19:52:24Z (the path list is factory-kept repository policy, test impact analysis first) and 2026-11-04T15:20:14Z (scope: the kit, both templates and every repository the factory creates; the one-gate rule restated as the fast tier for hooks and in-lane work, the full tier for merge readiness and CI). Today every ticket runs the full gate twice.
evidence: issue-lifecycle#lc-integrate 'The script merges, runs just check' and ADR 0017 'then runs that worktree's just check' against issue #503 consensus (comment 2026-11-03T19:44:38Z item 2: 'Fast-integrated heads are provisional ... a full gate for any ticket integration touching a listed path'). Marked weakens: a head integrated on the fast tier has not passed the full gate.

what: Adds the checkpoint rule (#lanes-checkpoints): the full gate on the candidate head at the pilot, on any integration touching the factory-kept shared-machinery list (adds, deletes, either side of a rename, old list plus new entries) or changing it, and on every lane's final head; each full pass recorded with head, gate configuration and list identity; the merge ask check refuses without a current final pass; a repository with no fast tier runs its own gate in full; the merge ask shows full-gate time against a gate-time budget, judged at review. Adds six criteria.
why: Owner ruling on issue #503 (2026-11-03, 'fully agree as a priority'), with the adversarial-review consensus (comment 2026-11-03T19:44:38Z, items 2 and 3) and the owner's corrections of 2026-11-03T19:52:24Z (the path list is factory-kept repository policy, test impact analysis first) and 2026-11-04T15:20:14Z (scope: the kit, both templates and every repository the factory creates; the one-gate rule restated as the fast tier for hooks and in-lane work, the full tier for merge readiness and CI). Today every ticket runs the full gate twice. Gate-time budget: owner/director comment 2026-11-04T15:24:06Z root cause 3 ('judged at review, not a timing check in the gate').
evidence: No issue-lifecycle clause names when the full gate must run or refuses a merge ask without a full pass on its head; issue #503 consensus item 2 ('Record head, gate configuration and policy identity; enforce the applicable checkpoints automatically and refuse merge-ask without current final proof').

what: CI alongside qc and review: as just qc and the review start on H the supervisor pushes H with the PR ready for review, so CI's full run goes in parallel; a push adding only qc's status-only commits starts no new CI full run, and the merge ask takes the checks of the head they follow under the existing status-only check. Adds story-no-redo and two criteria. Also relaxes CI on status-only commits: told to the director at once.
why: Owner direction on issue #586 (2026-11-05, split from #577 decision 6): after a lane merges main the redo costs about an hour (#503: 19 criteria re-judged, a delta review re-reading main's reviewed content, CI's ~15 min full run only after qc and review and again on qc's status-only commit). Director brief for lane gh586 (2026-11-05).
evidence: issue #586 item 3 against .github/workflows/check.yml (runs on every ready-PR push, draft PRs skipped, so CI starts only when the PR is marked ready at the merge ask and reruns its full ~15 min on qc's status-only commit) and octo-feather-lane merge-ask ('Checks: pending on head' until CI finishes on H'); no lanes-one-head clause places CI.

what: Review of a main merge that resolved a conflict covers that resolution alone (git show --remerge-diff, git's own tool): a clear verdict on it keeps the earlier review verdict, and the merge ask names the reviewed head, the merge and the resolution verdict; just qc on the new head re-judges only what moved (quality#qc-carry). gates-merge names the resolution review among the rerun gates. Adds one criterion. Also relaxes re-review (no full delta review after a main merge): told to the director at once.
why: Owner direction on issue #586 (2026-11-05, split from #577 decision 6): after a lane merges main the redo costs about an hour (#503: 19 criteria re-judged, a delta review re-reading main's reviewed content, CI's ~15 min full run only after qc and review and again on qc's status-only commit). Director brief for lane gh586 (2026-11-05).
evidence: issue #586 item 2 ('The delta review re-reads main's already-reviewed content') against issue-lifecycle#lanes-one-head, which keeps the review verdict only for a merge of main the check proves clean, so any resolved conflict means a full fresh review of the lane.

what: gates-merge points to #lanes-one-head for the resolution review's scope; lanes-one-head points to quality#qc-carry for what qc judges after a resolved merge, without restating it.
why: Code review of PR #608 at d0e4381 (class duplicated-rule, ADR 0008 rung 1): these clauses restated rules their owner anchors state; each now points to its owner.
evidence: review finding duplicated-rule: gates-merge 'a resolved conflict's review covering that resolution alone' and lanes-one-head 'judges again only the criteria that merge moved' restate #lanes-one-head and quality#qc-carry.

what: A ticket's demo path goes through a public interface the product offers its users (its CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP or another public protocol), the wording of quality#acceptance-public-surfaces, not the app's CLI, HTTP or UI only; lanes-tickets keeps the runnable-script fallback. Marked weakens: a ticket may now end on an MCP or other public-protocol demo.
why: Owner amendment to PR #797 before merge, 2026-11-12 (director relay): end-to-end tests and QC/QA demos go through the product's public interfaces of any kind (CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP or another public protocol it offers its users), not limited to the sites the lane first wrote; director ruling 2026-11-12: widen the ticket-demo sites in this lane, wording identical to quality#acceptance-public-surfaces.
evidence: issue-lifecycle#acceptance-tracer-tickets 'ends on a demo path through the app's CLI, HTTP or UI' and #lanes-tickets 'ending on a demo path through the app CLI, HTTP or UI' against quality#acceptance-public-surfaces at c2b2ac26 'an end-to-end test drives a public interface the product offers its users (its CLI, HTTP, UI, MCP or another public protocol)': a ticket for an MCP-only product cannot end on a demo the criterion allows.

what: A spec pull request no longer merges by the owner's hand: the owner approves it, the director relays the approval with the pull request's head to a supervisor it names, and that supervisor merges it pinned to that head; neither the owner nor the director merges it. gates-merge gains that sentence, lc-spec-pr's owner cell reads approves and its supervisor cell merges, and the two criteria whose scenario had the owner merging now read the owner approves and the named supervisor merges.
why: Owner ruling 2026-11-13, relayed by the director: spec pull requests merge like lane pull requests, the owner approves and a supervisor merges pinned; the merge gate stays the owner's (gates-list unchanged). The ruling was already applied to PR #827. Loud because it moves the merge action itself away from the owner.
evidence: lc-spec-pr put 'Gate: merges the spec pull request' in the Owner column and acceptance-kickoff-lanes read 'When the owner merges its spec pull request', contradicting the owner's ruling that the owner never merges; PR #827 (spec reporting-autonomy) was merged on owner approval by supervisor gh785 with gh pr merge 827 --merge --match-head-commit 04c0efcd7c82ea73a931fee152f34f3c011148ce, merge commit 5192232e385e8679a519c300c55108488aca6e46.

what: qc-interim and lc-qc: just qc takes STATUS... (one or more status files) before PR; one run judges the lane's criteria in every spec it builds, each id in exactly one named status file's spec, and commits only those status files in one commit (was: one STATUS, its status file).
why: One just qc run takes every status file the lane builds, so one final full gate and one status-only commit serve a lane building criteria in several specs, as lanes-one-head and qc-capture already require. Extends the existing just qc seam; no second mechanism. One STATUS keeps working as before.
evidence: Issue #858 (lane gh785, 2026-11-13): a lane building criteria in roles and comms ran `just qc` for roles, whose status-only commit moved the head, so `just qc` for comms found no gate records at the new head and judged 0/3 insufficient evidence; the lane needed a second ~8 min full gate. Contradiction: quality#qc-capture 'The final head's full gate runs each tagged test once ... that one execution counts both toward the full gate and as the criterion's record' and issue-lifecycle#lanes-one-head 'just qc, naming every criterion the lane builds' against the seam 'just qc STATUS PR ID...' (issue-lifecycle#qc-interim, quality#boundary-judge), which takes one status file.

what: A correction lane starts on a reflection-missed finding, not on each one, and while a class's correction-lane issue is open a new finding of the class is a comment on it, never a new issue (comms #reflection-correction). Criteria text unchanged.
why: Owner rule 2026-11-17 relayed by the director on lane gh851 (issue #851): a recurrence is a comment on the existing issue, never a new issue.
evidence: issue-lifecycle#lanes-correction 'A class that already has a correction-lane issue, open or closed, starts another only on a finding of that class dated after that issue closed' vs comms#reflection-correction 'for each reflection-missed finding, it files the correction lane's parent issue'; and the filer's output: 147 duplicate correction-lane issues closed by hand 2026-11-17 (/home/exedev/scratch/issue-triage/REPORT.md, cluster table and 'the filer itself'), scripts/octo-feather-reflect still_due skipping an open class with no trace (issue #851)
